ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a horizontal straight line passing through the central intersection point. In the upper half-plane of the central intersection point, from the left horizontal ray to the right horizontal ray, three adjacent angles labeled ∠1, 69°, and 47° in sequence, and they together form a straight angle on a straight line. The problem also gives the condition m∠4 = m∠5. Reasoning: Because ∠1, 69°, and 47° are above the same straight line and adjacent in sequence, their sum is 180°. Therefore ∠1 + 69° + 47° = 180°, so ∠1 = 180° - 69° - 47° = 64°. The condition m∠4 = m∠5 does not need to be used in this direct solving process.

method.method_draft: Read the image around the central intersection. The angle vertically opposite ∠3 is the combined upper-right angle made of 69° and 47°, so ∠3 = 69° + 47° = 116°. Since ∠1 and ∠3 lie on opposite sides of the same straight slanted line at the central intersection, they form a linear pair, so ∠1 + ∠3 = 180°. Thus ∠1 = 180° - 116° = 64°. The given m∠4 = m∠5 can be acknowledged as describing the lower triangle, but it is not required once ∠3 is obtained from vertical angles.
